chunks: 2909 - And Ishaq ibn Ammar narrated from Abu Ibrahim عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a wealthy woman who has performed the Hajj of Islam, then says to her husband, 'Take me for hajj once again.' Does he have the right to prevent her? He said: 'Yes. He may say to her: My right over you is greater than your right over me in this matter.'

key_terms.الْمَرْأَةِ: the woman under discussion in the ruling
key_terms.الْمُوسِرَةِ: a woman of financial means, able to afford the journey
key_terms.حَجَّةَ الْإِسْلَامِ: the obligatory hajj required once in a lifetime
key_terms.حَقِّي عَلَيْكِ: my right over you, referring to the husband's marital claim
key_terms.فِي ذَا: in this matter, limiting the statement to this case
key_terms.لِزَوْجِهَا: to her husband, indicating the marital context of the ruling

ai.seo_question: Can a husband prevent his wife from going on a non-obligatory hajj after she has already performed the obligatory Hajj of Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a married woman who has already fulfilled the obligatory hajj. It indicates that if she seeks to perform hajj again voluntarily, her husband may prevent her on the basis of his greater marital right in this specific matter.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2909 - Ishaq ibn Ammar narrated from Abu Ibrahim (as), who said:

I asked him about a wealthy woman who had already performed the Hajj of Islam but said to her husband, "Take me for Hajj again." Can he prevent her from going?
Imam (as) said: "Yes, he can say to her, 'My right over you is greater than your right over me in this matter.'"
